annotations.title: How much life insurance do I need?

description: How much life insurance do I need? Work it out with the DIME method (DIME = Debts, Income, Mortgage, Education — the four parts of the need, each in plain words), with every line shown: your debts, the years of pay your family would need, your mortgage, and school costs ahead, minus the savings and coverage you already have. Returns a coverage gap and the full math, not a rule of thumb. It runs the same deterministic size engine as the calculator on clearlinefamily.com, over eight money facts in dollars: yearly pay, a partner's yearly pay, years of pay to replace (the Check's standard guess is 10 when they do not say, and the result marks it as a guess), the mortgage still owed, other debts, school costs ahead, savings, and coverage already in place. Collect the facts in conversation first and ask about the ones people forget (school costs ahead, a partner's pay, savings, work coverage as a dollar amount); any fact not supplied is counted as not counted and named in the result, never silently assumed. A first number needs only three facts — yearly pay, years of pay to replace, and the mortgage still owed; call with just those for a starting gap, then refine it with the rest, each added fact named in the result. If no money fact has been given yet, the tool returns the DIME lines and the facts to collect instead of inventing a number. General education only: it names no company, recommends nothing, asks no health questions, and saves nothing you enter.

annual_income.description: Their yearly pay in dollars, before tax is fine. The spine of the gap: pay times years to replace.

existing_coverage.description: Coverage amount already in place, in dollars (work plus their own). Comes off the need. If they only know a multiple of pay, multiply it out before calling: 2 times a $140,000 pay is $280,000.

income_years.description: Years of pay the coverage should replace. If not given, the Check's standard guess of 10 years is used and marked as a guess in the result.

other_debts.description: Other debts to pay off, in dollars (cards, loans, anything but the mortgage).

partner_income.description: A partner's yearly pay in dollars, if a partner's pay also needs replacing.

savings.description: Savings or cash they could use, in dollars. Comes off the need.

school_costs.description: School costs ahead they plan to pay, in dollars. Blank counts as $0.
